maria: opened PR 5943 to tidy Nebula3b model card: add an 8k example in the sequence limits table, clarify "effective long-window" vs `max_context`, add a small SDK3 embed-shard + batch-helper example, and create redirects for two legacy bench CSV links. PTAL.
ryan: drop link pls
maria: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5943 
jin: quick skim: looks good. 2 tiny issues: the SDK3 example references `np.mean` but doesn't import numpy; and the batch-helper example might be clearer if we show the `.batch()` call returning embeddings directly.
eva: also add a note under Compatibility about quantized-variant routing. folks could misinterpret the bench numbers if they don't see which variant (fp16 vs q4) was measured.
sam: on the shard example, please add a short sentence that averaging is a simple merge strategy but not ideal for all retrieval workflows. maybe link to the retriever guidance page.
maria: will do. proposed snippet to insert into the card (SDK3 idiomatic):
```python
import numpy as np
from redwood import Client
cli = Client()
# preferred: batching helper (handles chunking + rate limits)
embs = cli.batch([long_doc]).embed(model="nebula3b-embed")
# manual shard + merge (appendix)
shards = [long_doc[i:i+1000] for i in range(0, len(long_doc), 1000)]
shard_embs = [cli.embed(model="nebula3b-embed", text=s) for s in shards]
merged = np.mean(shard_embs, axis=0)
# rolling-window generation for long documents
resp = cli.generate(model="nebula3b", prompt=long_doc, max_new_tokens=256, rolling_window=1024)
```
leah: nit: use `max_new_tokens` everywhere, yes. also please normalize bench labels to "tokens/sec" across the doc. one more ask: include an example row for 8k doc in the limits table so PMs can reference it in product docs.
maria: will add 8k row and bench-label normalization. adding Compatibility line: "Note: quantized variants may route to CPU fallback on certain small hosts; see runtime-fallback playbook and the fallback test script linked below for reproducible bench numbers." and link to playbook + script.*eva: that reads fine. small suggestion: in the compatibility blurb, call out which variants (nebula3b-fp16, nebula3b-q4) were used for which rows.
maria: good call. i'll annotate the table cells with variant tags.
